findings.statement: PROPOSED rank 1 mitigation clue: retain only the algebraic decomposition into an analytic transport/base Jacobian plus bounded gather-core-scatter updates, then use the factors in an exact linear solve or a separately validated linear preconditioner. The driver constructs an upwind transport block, differentiates a small moment/collision core, and returns LowRankJacobianFactors to a custom solve hook. This structure could isolate fast dissipative collision modes from a large angular-transport state, but the current bytes materialize the base as a dense state-by-state matrix and inject clipped approximate diagonals into the method Jacobian. Reuse therefore means re-deriving the block/operator structure, not translating the implementation. Prerequisites are an exact future Bianchi residual/JVP, prospectively bounded factor rank and conditioning, sparse or matrix-free storage of the base block, and dense-versus-factorized small-case identity checks. Falsifiers are rank growth comparable to the full state, failed linear residuals, changed convergence order or phase under the approximate Jacobian, or any failed conservation/covariance invariant.
assumptions_used: A future anisotropic kinetic discretization has a large transport block coupled through a comparatively small set of moments.

findings.statement: The current JAX bytes have no authority for coupled stiff, highly oscillatory Bianchi shear. The full driver rejects every nonzero Sigma_minus initial condition and hard-codes Pi_minus=0, so it cannot exercise the hypothesized coupled two-shear dynamics. Its adaptive calls expose rtol, atol, max_steps, and event refinement but no explicit maximum-step, local-frequency, zero-crossing, phase-lag, or oscillation-count constraint; the adjoint helpers default to predetermined uniform or log schedules whose error control is only an assumed step count. A linearly implicit W=I/(gamma h)-J solve is a stiffness mechanism clue, not evidence of phase fidelity. Reopen prerequisites are a prospective two-shear equation/observable contract, manufactured stiff-oscillatory tests, local-frequency and resonance sweeps, phase and amplitude convergence under step refinement, long-time numerical-damping bounds, invariant/positivity checks, and comparison to an independently implemented reference. Any local-error pass accompanied by nonconvergent phase, overdamping, missed zero crossings, or event-time drift is a falsifier.

Stiff stability and oscillatory phase resolution are separate numerical obligations.
